Cassava___Bacterial Blight (CBB).symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots, wilting of young shoots, gum exudation on stems, and premature leaf drop.
Cassava___Bacterial Blight (CBB).prevention: Use certified disease-free stem cuttings, plant resistant cassava varieties, implement crop rotation, and avoid overhead irrigation.

Cassava___Brown Streak Disease (CBSD).symptoms: Yellowing or chlorosis along secondary leaf veins, dark brown necrotic streaks on green stems, and dry corky necrosis within storage roots.
Cassava___Brown Streak Disease (CBSD).prevention: Plant virus-tested clean planting material, manage whitefly vector populations using integrated pest management, and rogue infected plants promptly.

Cassava___Green Mottle (CGM).symptoms: Irregular green mosaic patterns, mottling, puckering, and mild stunting on young emerging leaves.
Cassava___Green Mottle (CGM).prevention: Select healthy vegetative propagules, monitor vector activity, and maintain field sanitation.

Cassava___Healthy.symptoms: Foliage exhibits uniform deep green color with vigorous expansion, well-formed leaf lobes, and no visible lesions.
Cassava___Healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced soil fertility, optimal moisture management, and routine field scouting.

Cassava___Mosaic Disease (CMD).symptoms: Severe mosaic mottling, distorted, curled, and stunted leaf blades, and reduced root tuber yield.
Cassava___Mosaic Disease (CMD).prevention: Deploy resistant cultivars, eliminate whitefly breeding habitats, and eradicate infected plant debris.

Rice___BrownSpot.symptoms: Small, oval or circular dark brown spots on leaves with gray or whitish centers and a yellow halo.
Rice___BrownSpot.prevention: Ensure balanced soil nutrition (adequate potassium and silicon), avoid severe drought stress, and practice seed treatment.

Rice___Healthy.symptoms: Vibrant emerald green leaf blades without necrotic spotting, lesions, or insect tunneling.
Rice___Healthy.prevention: Follow recommended nitrogen schedules, maintain appropriate water depth, and monitor weed growth.

Rice___Hispa.symptoms: White parallel streaks on leaves caused by larval leaf tunneling, giving leaves a bleached appearance.
Rice___Hispa.prevention: Encourage natural predator populations, avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization, and practice sweep netting in early growth stages.

Rice___LeafBlast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped or elliptical lesions with grayish-white centers and brownish-red borders on leaf blades.
Rice___LeafBlast.prevention: Plant blast-tolerant rice varieties, avoid excessive nitrogen application, maintain proper field drainage, and space plants properly.

apple___apple scab.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown or black circular spots on leaves, becoming scabby and causing leaf puckering.
apple___apple scab.prevention: Prune tree canopies to improve airflow, rake and shred fallen leaves in autumn, and apply preventive organic fungicides during wet spring weather.

apple___black rot.symptoms: Small purple flecks enlarging into 'frog-eye' leaf spots with light brown centers and purple margins.
apple___black rot.prevention: Prune out dead wood, mummified fruits, and cankers during winter dormancy, and sterilize pruning tools between cuts.

apple___cedar apple rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish-orange spots on the upper leaf surface with tiny fungal tube projections underneath.
apple___cedar apple rust.prevention: Remove nearby eastern red cedar trees if practical, plant rust-resistant apple cultivars, and maintain orchard sanitation.

apple___healthy.symptoms: Intact, deep green leaves with crisp margins and absence of discoloration, fungal mycelium, or insect damage.
apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper tree nutrition, regular pruning for sun penetration, and periodic orchard monitoring.

cherry (including sour)___healthy.symptoms: Glossy green leaves free of chlorosis, necrosis, curling, or fungal powder.
cherry (including sour)___healthy.prevention: Ensure good soil drainage, timely dormant pruning, and regular canopy inspections.

cherry (including sour)___powdery mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth patches on young leaves and shoots, accompanied by upward leaf curling.
cherry (including sour)___powdery mildew.prevention: Prune suckers and interior canopy branches to optimize ventilation, and avoid late-season excessive nitrogen.

corn (maize)___cercospora leaf spot gray.symptoms: Rectangular, brown or grayish lesions restricted between parallel leaf veins.
corn (maize)___cercospora leaf spot gray.prevention: Rotate crops with non-grass crops (e.g. legumes), incorporate residue management, and select resistant corn hybrids.

corn (maize)___common rust.symptoms: Circular to elongate golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces.
corn (maize)___common rust.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids and plant early in the season to evade late-summer spore arrival.

corn (maize)___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant dark green leaves without pustules, stripes, or necrotic edges.
corn (maize)___healthy.prevention: Follow soil test-based fertilisation and scout fields during vegetative stages.

corn (maize)___northern leaf blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions on foliage.
corn (maize)___northern leaf blight.prevention: Select resistant hybrids, manage crop residue through conservation tillage, and practice crop rotation.

grape___black rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black pycnidia (spore bodies) scattered inside.
grape___black rot.prevention: Prune vines to open the canopy for airflow, remove mummified grape clusters, and avoid overhead sprinkler watering.

grape___esca (black measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' chlorotic and necrotic patterns between leaf veins and dark purple speckling on fruit berries.
grape___esca (black measles).prevention: Protect pruning wounds with wound sealants, avoid pruning during heavy rain periods, and remove severely declining vines.

grape___healthy.symptoms: Uniform lush green palmately lobed leaves free from fungal lesions, insect galls, or marginal necrosis.
grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain vine trellis architecture, balanced NPK fertigation, and proactive canopy management.

grape___leaf blight (isariopsis leaf spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown or black spots with well-defined margins, often causing early leaf senescence.
grape___leaf blight (isariopsis leaf spo.prevention: Improve airflow through leaf pulling in fruiting zones, remove diseased leaf litter, and ensure balanced nutrition.

orange___haunglongbing (citrus greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle on leaves, yellowing of veins, and stunted, bitter, lopsided fruit.
orange___haunglongbing (citrus greening).prevention: Control Asian citrus psyllid vector populations, use disease-free nursery stock from screenhouses, and eradicate infected trees.

peach___bacterial spot.symptoms: Angular, water-soaked purple or dark brown lesions on leaves, often dropping out to leave a 'shot-hole' appearance.
peach___bacterial spot.prevention: Plant tolerant peach cultivars, avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation, and plant protective windbreaks.

peach___healthy.symptoms: Lanceolate leaves with smooth serrated margins and vibrant green color free of spots or perforations.
peach___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular orchard pruning, balanced fertilization, and good soil drainage.

pepper, bell___bacterial spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, circular to irregular lesions with dark margins on leaves, causing defoliation.
pepper, bell___bacterial spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds, avoid working in fields when foliage is wet, and rotate with non-solanaceous crops.

pepper, bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy, dark green leaves with crisp edges, sturdy stems, and robust flowering.
pepper, bell___healthy.prevention: Employ drip irrigation, mulch beds to prevent soil splashing, and monitor for early pest signs.

potato___early blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions featuring characteristic concentric rings ('target board' pattern) on older leaves.
potato___early blight.prevention: Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium fertilization, practice a 3-year crop rotation, and avoid plant stress.

potato___healthy.symptoms: Compound leaves with rich green coloration and vigorous leaf turgor without blighted zones.
potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular hilling, optimal drip irrigation, and good field drainage.

potato___late blight.symptoms: Water-soaked, rapidly expanding dark green to purplish-black lesions with pale green borders and white mold underneath.
potato___late blight.prevention: Destroy cull piles, plant certified disease-free seed tubers, avoid leaf wetness, and harvest in dry weather.

squash___powdery mildew.symptoms: Talcum powder-like white fungal colonies expanding over both upper and lower leaf surfaces, causing premature yellowing.
squash___powdery mildew.prevention: Plant powdery mildew-resistant squash varieties, provide ample plant spacing, and ensure full sun exposure.

strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves with vibrant green sheen, intact serrated edges, and sturdy petioles.
strawberry___healthy.prevention: Use straw mulch to separate foliage from soil, manage drip lines carefully, and scout regularly.

strawberry___leaf scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, irregular purple or dark reddish spots without distinct white centers, causing leaf margins to curl and scorch.
strawberry___leaf scorch.prevention: Plant resistant strawberry varieties, maintain good bed spacing to accelerate leaf drying, and remove dead leaves post-harvest.

tomato___bacterial spot.symptoms: Small, dark brown, water-soaked circular spots with yellow halos that may merge and cause foliage loss.
tomato___bacterial spot.prevention: Use certified clean seed, avoid handling plants when wet, apply mulch to suppress soil splashing, and rotate crops.

tomato___early blight.symptoms: Brown to black lesions with concentric rings (target pattern) beginning on lower mature leaves and progressing upward.
tomato___early blight.prevention: Prune bottom leaves to avoid soil contact, stake plants for vertical growth, and water at the base with drip tape.

tomato___healthy.symptoms: Deep green, pinnately compound leaves with vigorous upright posture and no chlorotic or necrotic spots.
tomato___healthy.prevention: Ensure balanced nutrition, consistent soil moisture, adequate sunlight, and routine preventative scouting.

tomato___late blight.symptoms: Greasy, dark brown to olive lesions on leaves with white fuzzy sporulation on the underside under cool, humid conditions.
tomato___late blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering, destroy infected plant residues, select resistant tomato hybrids, and maintain wide spacing.

tomato___leaf mold.symptoms: Pale yellow or greenish chlorotic spots on upper leaf surfaces matching olive-green to brown velvety fungal patches underneath.
tomato___leaf mold.prevention: Improve greenhouse/field ventilation to keep relative humidity below 85%, and prune dense vegetative foliage.

tomato___septoria leaf spot.symptoms: Small, circular spots with dark brown margins and sunken grayish-white centers dotted with tiny black fruiting structures.
tomato___septoria leaf spot.prevention: Mulch the soil thoroughly beneath plants, remove lower blighted leaves, and avoid working among damp plants.

tomato___spider mites two-spotted spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or speckling on leaves, accompanied by delicate silk webbing on leaf undersides in hot, dry weather.
tomato___spider mites two-spotted spider.prevention: Encourage predatory mites, avoid excessive dust in fields, and wash foliage with water sprays during dry spells.

tomato___target spot.symptoms: Small brown circular lesions that expand with pinpoint concentric rings and light brown centers, leading to leaf drop.
tomato___target spot.prevention: Maintain proper plant spacing, eliminate solanaceous weeds around fields, and practice regular staking.

tomato___tomato mosaic virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, leaf distortion, blister-like leaf puckering, and severe stunting.
tomato___tomato mosaic virus.prevention: Disinfect tools with 10% trisodium phosphate or non-fat milk, wash hands thoroughly before handling plants, and plant resistant varieties.

tomato___tomato yellow leaf curl virus.symptoms: Marked upward curling of leaf margins, severe chlorosis/yellowing, reduction in leaf size, and stunted bushy growth.
tomato___tomato yellow leaf curl virus.prevention: Manage sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) populations with insect netting and yellow sticky traps, and deploy TYLCV-resistant cultivars.
